s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive lower extremity swelling and pain with evidence of deep vein thrombosis
salient_findings: Gradually progressive swelling, pain, and stiffness in the left lower leg
Tender, swollen, warm, and erythematous left lower leg
Extensive deep vein thrombosis on Doppler ultrasonography
key_facts: No fever, chest pain, shortness of breath, hemoptysis, or syncope
Medical history of three prior abortions
Recurrent microcytic anemia treated with iron supplementation
Two prior dilation and curettage procedures
No family history of thromboembolic disease
Bilateral dorsalis pedis pulses were palpable
Sensation was intact without ischemic changes
Hemoglobin 9.5 g/dL with an MCV of 63 fL

shortlist.label: Deep vein thrombosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has extensive deep vein thrombosis demonstrated by Doppler ultrasonography

shortlist.label: May-Thurner syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Compression of the left common iliac vein by the overlying right common iliac artery is consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Iliac vein compression syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's CT scan shows compression of the left common iliac vein, which is a key feature of this condition

shortlist.label: Post-thrombotic syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's history of deep vein thrombosis and symptoms of progressive lower extremity swelling and pain are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Antithrombin III deficiency
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's recurrent deep vein thrombosis despite lack of family history suggests a possible underlying coagulation disorder

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of extensive deep vein thrombosis and the CT scan finding of compression of the left common iliac vein by the overlying right common iliac artery are consistent with May-Thurner syndrome, a condition where the left common iliac vein is compressed by the right common iliac artery, leading to thrombosis.

rejected.label: Deep vein thrombosis
rejected.why: While the patient has deep vein thrombosis, this diagnosis does not explain the underlying cause of the thrombosis.

rejected.label: Iliac vein compression syndrome
rejected.why: This is a broader term that encompasses May-Thurner syndrome, but May-Thurner syndrome is a more specific diagnosis that fits the patient's presentation.

rejected.label: Post-thrombotic syndrome
rejected.why: This condition occurs after a DVT has resolved, leading to chronic symptoms, but the patient's presentation is more consistent with an acute DVT.

rejected.label: Antithrombin III deficiency
rejected.why: There is no indication of a coagulopathy or a family history of thromboembolic disease that would suggest antithrombin III deficiency as the primary diagnosis.
